To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the perceptions of grassland improvement and degradation are not uniform among semi-pastorists in China, but vary according to the different uses of grassland and their corresponding perceptions of the ecological state.
the local perception of grassland degradation is a function of the institutional credibility of the state’s land management policies and endogenous knowledge of grassland management.
(1) pastoral mobility and ecological knowledge are both crucial for grassland management; and (2) the perceptions of grassland management among semi-pastorialist communities in Ningxia are divergent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: how can the credibility of institutions be enhanced in the face of epistemic diversity?
how the institutional credibility of grassland governance is affected by epistemic diversity.
the epistemological diversity of knowledge and the implications for institutional credibility in the context of grassland management.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the institutional credibility of grassland policies in China is not only dependent on their legitimacy in relation to local power dynamics, but also on their epistemic legitimacy in relation to endogenous knowledge.
the epistemic diversity in the perception of degradation among local communities in China is an outcome of the interplay of local knowledge and institutional credibility.
the epistemic diversity of the local communities in the study area has a significant influence on the credibility of institutions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the institutional credibility of grassland management in the two regions can be improved through more participatory approaches that take into account the local perceptions of degradation and the epistemological diversity of actors involved.

, while the institutionalization of environmental knowledge can be a powerful tool for the implementation of environmental policies, the institutionalization of epistemic diversity may be a more effective approach for sustainable environmental governance.

, while the ‘Land’ papers have explored the role of land in the making of the nation and the state in the context of colonialism and imperialism, the ‘Resources’ papers have explored how local actors and institutions interact in resource management, and how the state is implicated in these interactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the credibility of institutions depends on the extent to which the institutional arrangements reflect the local perceptions of the problem at hand, which are in turn shaped by the local perceptions of environmental change.
the epistemic and institutional diversity of the Chinese grasslands should be taken seriously in order to improve policy outcomes.
, in order to be effective, institutional credibility needs to be built upon the epistemic diversity of the actors involved in the institutional process.
